title: US equity markets closed — Christmas observed (Christmas Day is a SATURDAY in 2027, so there is NO Christmas Eve half session)
source: EST: weekday arithmetic plus the NYSE's own observed precedent, not a fetched 2027 exchange calendar. Christmas Day 2027 falls on SATURDAY 2027-12-25, and the NYSE observes a Saturday holiday on the preceding Friday, which is 2027-12-24. THE PRECEDENT WAS VERIFIED FROM MARKET DATA THIS SESSION RATHER THAN ASSERTED: 2021 is the only other Saturday-Christmas year in the 2020-12-01 to 2026-09-04 tape, and the SPY daily session series fetched direct from stockanalysis.com (246,812 bytes, 2026-09-08) jumps straight from 2021-12-23 to 2021-12-27 -- Friday 2021-12-24 is not a session at all. THE SECOND HALF OF THIS ENTRY MATTERS MORE THAN THE CLOSURE. In a Saturday-Christmas year there is also NO 1:00 p.m. ET Christmas Eve half session, because the day that would carry it is the closure itself. The same tape confirms the pattern in both directions: Christmas Eve half sessions exist in the window only on 2020-12-24, 2024-12-24 and 2025-12-24 (Dec 24 a Thursday, Tuesday and Wednesday), and are absent in 2021, 2022 and 2023 (Dec 25 a Saturday, Sunday and Monday). Filed estimate on the same taxonomy limit the labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26 and memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 entries documented: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for an exchange's own holiday calendar, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the egress proxy blocks nyse.com outright. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Discovered during the consumer-confidence-2027-12-22 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-12-22 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08) and PROPOSED BECAUSE IT IS LOAD-BEARING, not merely adjacent. The proposer's leg 5 tests whether the post-print Christmas corridor's range compression is a half-session artifact -- the same test that collapsed the consumer-confidence-2027-11-30 lane's post-Thanksgiving finding into 'it is Black Friday'. It is not: removing the corridor's two half sessions leaves the compression at 8 of 9. But whoever takes THIS id should know the arithmetic that made the question askable, because it is the one structural fact that separates December 2027 from December 2024, 2025 and 2026. THREE CAUTIONS. (1) THE ABSENCE IS THE FINDING, so do not file a companion christmas-eve-half-day-2027-12-24 -- there is no half session in 2027 and such an entry would be a false calendar row. Contrast christmas-eve-half-day-2026-12-24, which is real because Christmas 2026 is a Friday. (2) THE CLOSURE IS ALSO WHY 2027'S YEAR-END CORRIDOR IS SHORT ONE SESSION on each side of it, so a lane counting sessions between this print and year-end from a 2024/2025 template will be off by one. (3) DO NOT PROMOTE THIS OFF A NEWS AGGREGATOR. The promotion venue is nyse.com's own holiday-closure table or SIFMA's recommendations panel, both currently egress-blocked from this lane's runner; a NEWS: prefix would be a downgrade, not a confirmation. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
